text.p: These are leading stories in this morning's Paris newspapers. LES ECHOS
-- February new car registrations down 24.6 percent after tumbling 33.6 percent in January.

-- Finance Minister Jean Arthuis' commitment to bring the public deficit to 2.8 percent of GDP in 1998 seems optimistic without finding new income similar to the transfer of funds from France Telecom, used to meet the 1997 deficit ratio target.
-- Elf Aquitaine to wind up Gabon financial subsidiary CPIH and distribute some three billion francs in dividends to stakeholders.
-- Belgian Prime Minister Jean-Luc Dehaene asks European Commission to examine whether Renault's shutdown of the Vilvoorde assembly plant violates EU social legislation.
-- Alcatel Alsthom ex-chairman Pierre Suard goes on trial today for alleged misuse of corporate funds.
-- Societe Generale opens branch office in Zagreb.
LA TRIBUNE
-- Aerospatiale , Alcatel Alsthom and Dassault finalised a secret deal in late January to share out Thomson-CSF in the event they win control in a relaunched privatisation.
-- Budget Minister Alain Lamassoure and Budesbank President Hans Tietmeyer expect economic activity to pick up this spring in their respective countries.
-- Credit Agricole says 1996 net profits will top 1995's 6.5 billion francs.
L'AGEFI
-- President Jacques Chirac expresses support for Portugal's bid to join the single currency at the outset, provided it meets entry criteria.
-- Caisse des Depots predicts 0.5 percent Q1 GDP growth.
LE FIGARO-ECONOMIE
-- Bank of France and financial institutions agree on ground rules for switch to Euro on money markets.
-- Appeal likely to be filed within 10 days against Paris court ruling to liquidate Comipar-Pallas Stern.
LIBERATION (Economic section)
-- LVMH says 650 million francs of exceptional items will impact 1996 results. THE INTERNATIONAL HERALD TRIBUNE
-- Dehaene calls for laws to prevent companies from moving plants as Belgium moves to sue Renault over Vilvoorde shutdown.
